statement: The cube of a whole number is 704969. Which number is it?

choices.misconception: I guessed that a cube starting with 7 comes from a number in the seventies and picked the choice ending in 9, without cubing 80 or 90 to check the size.
I thought a cube ending in 9 must come from a number ending in 3, because 3 squared ends in 9, mixing up squares with cubes.
I made two slips: I thought the number ends in 3, and taking 90 cubed as 72900 I placed it above 90.
I took 90 cubed as 72900 instead of 729000, so I thought the number was above 90, and then picked the choice ending in 9.

hints: Two cheap tests: the size of the number and its last digit.
Trap the number between two multiples of 10 by cubing them, then decide its last digit from the last digit of the cube. Only one choice can pass both tests.
80 cubed is 512000 and 90 cubed is 729000. Which single digit, cubed, ends in 9?

solutions.reliable: 80 cubed = 512000 and 90 cubed = 729000, so the number lies between 80 and 90. The last digits of the cubes of 0 to 9 are 0, 1, 8, 7, 4, 5, 6, 3, 2, 9, all different, and only 9 cubed ends in 9. So the number ends in 9 and lies between 80 and 90: it is 89. Indeed 89 x 89 x 89 = 704969. The transferable idea: two quick bounds, one on size and one on the last digit, can eliminate every wrong choice without the full calculation.

whyOnTest: Bounding by size and by last digit rules out every wrong choice without a long multiplication, which is the core of eliminating impossible answers.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
